plan.name: Reject unfixable Go acceptance tests
plan.summary: Tighten built-in Go plan checking so a completed compilation failure qualifies only when source-based analysis attributes every error in the acceptance files to missing or changed production APIs, including undefined names or selectors and incompatible production calls or types. Refuse unused imports or locals, syntax errors, test-local type errors and mixtures of these with legitimate API errors, retaining the source location and compiler diagnostic in the planner's feedback. Stage a dedicated Go analysis helper with the built-in sandbox runner, inspect internal and external tests without executing their initialization, and preserve compiled failing tests, attributable API failures, production-only corrections requiring runtime passes, and the existing offline execution, budgets and interruption rules. Extend the existing sandbox check tests to document the narrower compilation rule while preserving their missing-API and runtime-failure controls. Update SPEC.md and docs/factory.md to describe this rule, citing the existing plumbing-plan and sandbox decisions D-0107 and D-0281; whoever merges records the new decision refining those rules, since the build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestBuiltinGoRefusesUnfixableAcceptance733
tests.says: Built-in Check refuses unused imports, unused locals, syntax errors and test-local type errors in internal and external acceptance tests, with the offending file and diagnostic in feedback.

tests.name: TestBuiltinGoRefusesMixedCompilerErrors733
tests.says: A missing production API cannot hide an immutable acceptance error in the same test, a helper declaration or another pinned file in its package; the refusal identifies that error.

tests.name: TestBuiltinGoDistinguishesRepairableFailures733
tests.says: Missing production functions, types and methods, changed production signatures and field types, and compiled assertion failures still qualify; production-only fixes make the unchanged tests pass, while adding a test-local type error refuses the draft.
